title: Split-on-Share Mirror code allocation
hypothesis: Allocating a compact shared-basis View first and adding private residuals only when reconstruction error exceeds a frozen threshold delays physical growth while retaining task quality versus always-private storage.
physical_object: shared rank-3 linear task basis with sequentially arriving task deltas
mirror_coordinate: per-task coefficients over the shared basis; private sparse residual allocated on threshold crossing
logical_multiplicity: ten task functions, including four later tasks with novel sparse directions
controls: generic PCA with same split policy

development.selection_metric: query NRMSE, split count and actual payload bytes

storage.authority: actual serialized payload bytes; indices, values, shared basis, codes and metadata charged
paid_objects: private residual indices int16 and values float32

success_gate: Adaptive policy retains query NRMSE <=0.05, splits all four novel tasks, and saves >=20% bytes versus always-private task vectors.
failure_gate: Threshold misses late novel tasks or adaptive payload fails to improve bytes at matched quality; equality with generic PCA means no Mirror-specific result.
boundaries: No continual optimization, forgetting, routing or natural task evidence
Threshold fixed at 0.15 before fresh evaluation
